corpusSummary: Corpus spans 2026 social-science papers on large language models across human–AI interaction, health, climate, education, and AI-as-research-tool uses. It reveals growing deployment of LLMs as experimental co-investigators, tutors, and policy aids, alongside rigorous evaluation of trust, empathy, representation, and safety. Common tensions include algorithmic bias, hallucinations, misinformation, transparency, and energy costs, with calls for validation frameworks, ethics, and equity-focused governance.

themes.name: AI as a research tool and methodological innovation
themes.description: Papers show LLMs are increasingly used as research tools and co-investigators across methods (coding, frame development, simulations, policy analysis), while raising concerns about validation, transparency, energy use, and ethics.

themes.name: Human–AI interaction, trust, empathy, and social dynamics
themes.description: Across education, health, and consumer contexts, research investigates trust, perceived humanness versus empathy, disclosure, social influence, and adoption dynamics in human–AI interactions.

themes.name: AI in education and learning: literacy, pedagogy, and assessment
themes.description: A substantial portion addresses AI’s role in education—teacher adoption, AI tutoring, language learning, and assessment—highlighting potential learning gains and risks like overreliance and ethical considerations.

themes.name: AI in health and wellbeing: information, education, and decision making
themes.description: Studies cover AI-generated health misinformation, patient education materials, clinical reasoning influences, and equity-focused governance in digital health contexts.

themes.name: Fairness, safety, and governance of LLMs across domains
themes.description: Research evaluates bias, safety, and governance—ranging from fairness in library reference services to misinformation warnings and ethical guidelines for AI deployment.

emergingKeywords: trust, humanness, and empathy in LLMs
